newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey explains north Iraq raids to U.N..
newsitem.headline: Turkey explains north Iraq raids to U.N..

text.p: Turkey has sent a letter to U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan to explain Ankara's frequent cross-border operations into northern Iraq against Kurdish rebels, a Turkish foreign ministry official said on Thursday.

"The foreign minister (Tansu Ciller) sent a letter to the U.N. secretary general to give a general response to Iraq's continuing complaints to the United Nations about the operations," the official told Reuters.
The letter was sent last month, he said.
Turkey last week sent troops backed by air support into northern Iraq to pursue Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels who have bases there. Military sources said 115 guerrillas died.
An Iraqi official newspaper on Wednesday condemned Ankara's drives into the region, saying that they were against the U.N. charter, international law and the spirit of good-neighbourliness.
The Turkish official said Ciller's letter informed Annan that Turkey respects Iraq's integrity and sovereignty but that it will continue to cross the border for security reasons.
The PKK uses bases in northern Iraq, outside Baghdad's control since 1991, as part of its 12-year-old guerrilla war for self-rule in southeastern Turkey.
More than 21,000 people have died in the conflict. Turkish troops have crossed into Iraq several times in large numbers.
Kurdish-held northern Iraq, shielded by Western allied airforce, broke away from Baghdad shortly after the 1991 Gulf War.
